description: Price holding, matching, or beating the market rate on a bank's deposits: annual cost, balances at risk, breakeven retention, and sensitivity. Free; computed from FFIEC filings; results state whether each number is filed, derived, or assumed.

baselineRunoffPercent.description: The share of the repriced balances that leaves within a year even when your rate matches the market. Your assumption, not a filed figure; a starting value to replace.

category.description: Which filed deposit category the pricing decision applies to. Balances and current cost come from the bank's Call Report.

certificate.description: FDIC certificate number of the bank.

leadPremiumBp.description: How far above the market rate the Lead option prices, in basis points. A starting value to replace with your own.

marketRatePercent.description: The rate competitors pay for this product. Leave empty to use the FDIC national average for the product as a reference; that average is usually well below competitive offers, so enter your own market rate when you have one.

replacementSpreadBp.description: What it costs, above the Fed funds rate, to replace balances that leave, in basis points.

repricedSharePercent.description: The part of the category balance whose rate changes under Match or Lead. For time deposits, use the share maturing soon (see the maturity wall calculator).

runoffPerPointPercent.description: The additional share of balances lost for every 100 basis points your rate sits below the market, and recovered for every 100bp above it. This is the elasticity assumption that drives the decision; the sensitivity table shows how the answer changes with it.
